1.why: All ten screens are static, flat pages with no animations, carousels, modals or pop-ups; only calm cards and a stepper.

2.why: Page title, the highlighted blue 'Next step' callout and the single dark-blue primary button stand out clearly, though the large black 'Activity logs' box draws attention away from the task.

3.why: Each step presents one heading, one or two fields and one obvious primary button, so the needed action is quick to locate, but the technical simulation log adds irrelevant content to scan.

4.why: Every screen restates the next step, the password policy and the codes are shown on-screen, so little must be held in memory, although the flow is still 8 steps with a very long hex recovery code to transfer.

5.why: No 'remember me' checkbox, biometric option or password-manager/autofill affordance appears; the only automation is a 'Fill recovery code field' button and a prefilled email at sign-in.

6.why: The sign-in page shows her email already filled in (helena@hospital.test), the stepper labels persist across pages, and previously delivered codes remain visible in the activity log.

7.why: Sentences are short, plain and generously sized, e.g. 'This is a calm, step-by-step process. You can stop and return later.'

8.why: No error or validation state appears in any of the ten screenshots, so there is no evidence that error messages explain the problem and the fix.

9.why: The actual codes to enter are displayed on the page and the password policy is listed, but no worked example of a valid password or input format is provided.

10.why: The authentication options used (new password, delivery authorization code, recovery code, one-time security code) are each clearly labelled with a heading and instruction, though no alternative such as face login exists.

11.why: Each screen offers a single primary action plus at most one secondary link, never presenting multiple competing choices.

12.why: Outcomes are explicitly confirmed ('Password saved. Your new password is ready to use.', 'Appointment request confirmed'), reinforced by the highlighted current stepper chip and the activity log.

13.why: Every page carries a 'Next step:' tip, a persistent 'Help and safe authentication' expander and a safety reminder line.

14.why: Recovery links such as 'Use a different email address', 'Reset password instead', 'Return to sign in' and 'Return to account recovery start' allow retrying, plus 'No time limit. You may return when ready.', though no explicit back/undo per step is visible.

15.why: All ten screens reuse the same header, stepper, card layout, button styling, safety reminder and footer text, making the pattern highly predictable.
